solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mostly less sound? Nonsense!

indicators.note: nonsense suggests the letters make no sense as they stand and must be rearranged
mostly means nearly all of the word, so the final letter of less is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a claim that there is less noise than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims less to LES; 'Nonsense!' shuffles LES with SOUND. The whole clue is the definition too: the quality in question is the very opposite of 'less sound', so the claim is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Volume of noise is the opposite of having less sound, which the clue jokingly dismisses as nonsense.

clue.text: Rig Labour outcome in London Mayoral election, needing leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their opening letters, so the first letter of each word from outcome to needing is taken

explanation.surface: A political story about the result for the Labour party in the race to be Mayor of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rig' looks like a verb meaning to fix the election; it is an oil rig, and 'Rig Labour' means the workforce on one.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers employed on drilling platforms in the petroleum industry are the labour force of a rig.

clue.text: Worst of anything I kept at home

indicators.note: kept at a place means held within it, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: Someone admits the worst thing they kept in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Of children, the naughtiest are the worst behaved, so the superlative of badness fits.

clue.text: Start to enjoy small boy colouring in

indicators.note: in places the colouring inside the shortened name

parts.note: GEO is a short form of the boy's name George, a small version of the name
a tint is a colouring

explanation.surface: A young lad takes up colouring-in as a pastime he begins to like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small boy' suggests a child; it is a shortened boy's name, GEO for George.
explanation.definitionFit: To get into a hobby is an idiom for beginning to like it and becoming involved.

clue.text: Nice you-and-us knot

parts.note: Nice is a French city, so the French for you, tu, is wanted
us is the newspaper itself, the Financial Times, abbreviated FT

explanation.surface: A pleasant knot tying the reader and the newspaper together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective; it is the French city, signalling French. 'us' is the setter's newspaper, the FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A clump or knot of hair, feathers or grass is a tuft.

clue.text: This side's armoured division, slightly modified, is militarily superior

indicators.note: slightly modified says the letters of the phrase are rearranged a little, here just two swapped

parts.note: our side's armoured division is our tanks

explanation.surface: Our side's tank division, given small upgrades, now has the edge on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the R and T of OUR TANKS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrank someone is to hold a higher military rank, being superior in the chain of command.

clue.text: Art nouveau brown furniture material

indicators.note: nouveau, French for new, asks for a new arrangement of the letters of the word before it

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Brown Art Nouveau furniture made from some cane-like material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art nouveau' reads as the design movement; 'nouveau' is the anagram signal on ART, giving RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Canes of a climbing palm are woven into chairs and tables, a classic material for furniture.

clue.text: Apply antiseptic in US to aide in distress

indicators.note: distress here is a verb, to rough up or damage, so the preceding words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: In America, a medical assistant in trouble needs antiseptic applied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' reads as a phrase meaning troubled, but the 'in' is part of the fodder TO AIDE IN. The verb is mainly American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating a wound with the antiseptic element iodine is a chiefly American verb for applying it.

clue.text: Palatine pendants from return address in Arab state

indicators.note: in puts the turned piece inside the state's initials

parts.note: UAE is the United Arab Emirates

indicators.note: return means the word for an address is sent back, read right to left

parts.note: luv is an informal form of address, as in 'all right, luv?'

explanation.surface: Royal pendants from the Palatine court are sent back to an address in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palatine' suggests a count's court; here it means of the palate. 'return' turns the word for an address round to VUL before it goes 'in' the state.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lobes hanging at the back of the soft palate are pendants of the palate, the plural of uvula.

clue.text: Eat modish goulash, not as hot as before

indicators.note: a goulash is a stew of mixed ingredients, so the letters are mixed up
not says the letters of the following words are taken out of the mixture

explanation.surface: Diners are told to eat a fashionable goulash, which is milder than it used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goulash' mixes the letters and 'not' takes out those of 'as hot'. 'as before' looks like part of the surface comparison but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin for 'the same', used in references to mean the same source as previously cited.

clue.text: Reject Italian silver clothing for young socialites

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the turned pair dresses the brood
to reject is to throw back, so the two abbreviations are turned round

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a litter is a brood of young animals

explanation.surface: Throw out the Italian silver clothes bought for young party-goers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' turns the two abbreviations round to GATI, which goes round the brood as 'clothing'. 'young socialites' reads as one phrase, but 'young' is a brood of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The fashionable rich and famous set who frequent glamorous parties are celebrated socialites.

clue.text: Separatist agent's revolutionary note

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned over completely, so the banknote word is read backwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: A spy for a separatist cause possesses a rebel's message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separatist agent' suggests a political operative; it is the agent that separates milk into curds and whey.
explanation.definitionFit: This enzyme preparation curdles milk, separating curds from whey in cheesemaking, so it is a separating agent.

clue.text: Pressing to boycott grand investiture

indicators.note: to boycott is to shun, so the grand is left out of the word

parts.note: thronging is crowding in, pressing together
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Urging people to shun a lavish ceremony of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' reads as urging; it means crowding round.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting someone on a throne is an act of installing them in office, a form of investiture.

clue.text: Tries again to open all lady solicitors practices

parts.note: to rehear a case is to try it again in court

indicators.note: the letters that open each word are their first letters

explanation.surface: A legal case is heard again to open up women's solicitor firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practices' looks like law firms; it means run-throughs. 'Tries' is a court trying a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-throughs before a performance are practice sessions, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Tried by state during Seed Riots

indicators.note: during means inside, so the verb goes within the scrambled letters
riots throw things into disorder, so the letters of the seed word are scrambled

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone was put on trial by the state for their part in the Seed Riots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riots' scrambles the seed word to ESED, and 'during' puts the verb for state inside it after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is a formal verb meaning to attempt it, so attempted is the sense.

clue.text: Staggered about, shaken but not a bit stirred

indicators.note: about means around, so the amazed word wraps round the trimmed one

parts.note: staggered means amazed, awed

indicators.note: not a bit tells us a small piece, the opening pair of letters, is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: A James Bond echo: a drink shaken, not stirred, and someone reeling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not a bit' drops the opening two letters, leaving AKEN, which 'about' places inside. The cocktail order 'shaken, not stirred' is evoked, but 'stirred' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred can mean roused from sleep, the same sense as woken up.

clue.text: Gradual start to pain she's suffering

indicators.note: suffering suggests pain twisting things about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: she's here gives the letters of she, the 's is the verb is

explanation.surface: A woman is in pain, and it is starting slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Introducing something in stages is a gradual way to start it.

clue.text: Feverishly prise end off ring of stimulator

indicators.note: feverishly means in a frenzied way, so the letters are agitated into a new order
end off says the last letter of the following word is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone frantically tries to lever the end off a ring on a stimulating device.
explanation.walkthrough: RING loses its end, G, to give RIN, shuffled with PRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: One who motivates or arouses enthusiasm in others is a stimulator.

clue.text: Maybe runner has to reserve soft seat

parts.note: a runner bean is one kind of bean
to bag a seat is slang for reserving it

explanation.surface: An athlete must save a comfortable chair for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete; it is a runner bean, a common British climbing bean.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cushion filled with beads or pellets forms a squashy chair, a soft seat.

clue.text: Remembers central alliance finally left prime minister ready for war

indicators.note: central means the middle letters of the word are taken
left means departed, so that letter is removed from the statesman's name

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British prime minister from 1945 to 1951

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of alliance

explanation.surface: A memory of the core alliance leaving a prime minister prepared for conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle three letters of Remembers give EMB. ATTLEE loses E, the final letter of alliance, which 'left' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw up troops in battle order is to prepare them for fighting, readying for war.

clue.text: Opening posh charcuterie houses

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the cured goods contain the upper-class letter

parts.note: charcuterie is cured or cooked meats
U means upper class, posh

explanation.surface: A smart delicatessen is opening up shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like a shop launch; it is an anatomical passage.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomical passage or channel such as the outer end of the urethra is an opening in the body.

clue.text: Music from the meeting of Super Mario and Sonic the Hedgehog

indicators.note: the meeting of the two names means only the letters where they join are kept, the outer ends of each name falling away

explanation.surface: A soundtrack from a crossover of two famous video game characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Join MARIO and SONIC and the answer straddles the junction: drop M at the front and NIC at the back. Super Mario and Sonic the Hedgehog are rival video game mascots.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodious style of song or passage between recitative and aria is a kind of vocal music.

clue.text: Unmoved by reins, it understood a bit

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase is a small piece lying across its words

explanation.surface: Holding the reins, a rider realised that the horse was a bit stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its original place, so something left there is unmoved.

clue.text: Seven Latin playing cards, usually

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: Seven Latin speakers are playing cards as they normally do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing cards' reads as a single phrase; 'playing' is the anagram signal and 'cards' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokens of love sent on 14 February usually take the form of greeting cards.

clue.text: Unruly Tory apprentice

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the party member are disordered

explanation.surface: A rebellious Conservative trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner or novice still learning a trade is a learner, like an apprentice.

clue.text: Dodgy dealer's return from knobs

indicators.note: return from means the word for big shots is read backwards

parts.note: knobs is slang for nobs, important people, VIPs

explanation.surface: A shady trader's profit from selling door knobs.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is a British slang figure, a flashy small-time black-market trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashy petty crook trading in black-market goods is a classic shady dealer.

clue.text: Arrogance contracted by high-end film maker

indicators.note: contracted by means made smaller by losing that letter

parts.note: hauteur is haughty arrogance

indicators.note: end here means the final letter of the word high, which is the one lost

explanation.surface: A haughty high-end film director signed up for a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-end' reads as luxury; it is the end letter of high. 'contracted' suggests signing a deal but means shrunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A director whose personal style shapes the whole work is regarded as the creator of a film.

clue.text: Recipient of parcel from totally extravagant phone company

parts.note: all means totally, as in all alone
OTT, over the top, means extravagant
EE is a British mobile phone network

explanation.surface: A delivery comes from a wildly lavish telecoms firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parcel' looks like a package; it is a parcel of land, as in an allotment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given a share or plot of land in an allocation is the receiver of that portion.
